palettes.name: Marmalade
palettes.note: Vermilion top against teal bottom is the whole idea. Hair is the top colour in shadow (oxblood), so it never reads as a fifth hue. Accent is held back for tongue, iris and laces.

palettes.name: Two-Ink Funnies
palettes.note: Only red and blue were on the press. Skin is red at roughly 40% tint, accent is where the two inks overlap (purple), and hair is the ink itself. Three real colours, six roles.

palettes.name: Night Shift
palettes.note: Printed on dark stock: violet carries the mass, magenta is the single saturated hit, and gold does double duty as hair and accent. The stock white (eyes, gloves) becomes the brightest thing on the sheet.

palettes.name: Bubblegum Ledger
palettes.note: Every fill lives in the top third of lightness. Plum ink is the only dark value, so it does all the structural work; hair is the ink. Sweet colour, sour line.

palettes.name: Moss & Mustard
palettes.note: Olive, rust and mustard all lean yellow, none is cleaner than about 60% saturation. Quiet on purpose: the drawing has to carry the character, not the colour.

palettes.name: Blueprint
palettes.relationship: One hue in three values + a spark
palettes.note: Navy ink, cobalt top, sky bottom, pale ground: one hue in four values. Orange appears only on the accent, so it reads as a signal. Hair is the ink.

palettes.name: Pine & Rosewater
palettes.note: Green against dusty rose, both held at mid value. The straw accent sits between them so it bridges rather than shouts. Hair and ink share one pine-black.

palettes.name: Lilac Hour
palettes.note: Coral and sun against periwinkle on a lilac ground. This is the deep-skin test palette: ink lines have to stay legible on S5, so ink is pushed to the darkest value in the set.

assignment_rules: accent: tongue, iris, jewel, hem, laces, hat band
skin: any ramp step in any palette
wonk: at most one, by the generator
